answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any supplier transition (switch_primary_vendor) carries unacceptable delivery risk this cycle—memory_c2 explicitly documents SLA misses in 3 of 4 quarters from the low-cost alternative, which would be catastrophic against a no-buffer schedule. Meanwhile finance's 18% spend cut mandate needs an immediate lever, and memory_c4 shows that benchmarking and renegotiating at renewal previously recovered real margin on both price and terms without any integration disruption (consistent with memory_c1's stability record and memory_c6's volume-pricing precedent). Negotiating terms with the incumbent ahead of the 14-day deadline addresses the cost mandate while preserving continuity of supply, deferring the higher-risk sourcing diversification (add_second_source per memory_c3) or vendor switch to a future cycle when there's more schedule slack to absorb transition risk. I verified c4 and c2 specifically because they carry the most weight for this decision: one supports the chosen path's feasibility, the other flags the key risk in the rejected alternative.
